category.label: ZMC
category.comparisonNote: ZMC means zinc + magnesium + calcium. Compare cost per label serving and each declared elemental mineral separately; the three mineral masses are not added into a single strength score.

guide.title: ZMC: assess zinc, magnesium and calcium separately
guide.summary: A three-mineral tablet is a formulation choice, not a single active ingredient with one meaningful strength score.
guide.evidence: Each mineral has established nutritional roles. Evidence about individual nutrients does not demonstrate that every ZMC combination improves outcomes.
guide.limitations: This guide makes no combination-specific efficacy claim. Product ratios, baseline diet, clinical need and co-ingredients differ; ZMA studies are not evidence for calcium-containing ZMC products.
guide.catalogReading: Review the elemental amount of each mineral, the label serving and its cost. Do not add their masses into a combined value score or treat calcium-salt weight as elemental calcium.
guide.safety: Check overlapping supplements and medicines. Excess zinc can affect copper status; calcium and magnesium can interfere with absorption of some medicines.
guide.author: Supplement Research editorial synthesis
bodySteps: The tablet releases separate calcium, magnesium and zinc compounds in the digestive tract.
Intestinal absorption and regulation differ for each mineral; vitamin D supports active calcium absorption.
Calcium supports bone and signalling functions, magnesium supports enzyme activity, and zinc supports many cellular processes.
guide.treatment: An appropriate individual mineral can correct its deficiency. This is not evidence that a ZMC combination cures osteoporosis, low testosterone or a general immunity problem.
guide.whoMayBenefit: Someone with assessed needs for the included minerals may consider a combination if its amounts fit the plan; a single deficient nutrient may need a different product.
guide.routineUse: No universal requirement for a three-mineral stack. Review each mineral separately and check overlap with other supplements.

whoCanConsider: Adults whose separate calcium, magnesium and zinc assessments identify needs that match a combination product.
People simplifying an established mineral plan after checking amounts and duplication with a clinician or dietitian.
whoShouldReview: Kidney disease, kidney-stone history or high blood calcium requires review.
Levothyroxine, oral bisphosphonates and certain antibiotics can interact with mineral supplements.
Existing mineral products need a total-intake check, including zinc exposure and copper balance.
buyingGuide.foodSummary: ZMC is three nutrients combined in a product. A varied diet supplies the minerals in different proportions; it need not reproduce a tablet's ratio.

dos.title: Check each mineral separately
dos.detail: Read elemental calcium, magnesium and zinc on the same verified label-serving basis.

dos.title: Review the complete combination
dos.detail: Check co-vitamins and existing products; a fixed combination should fit the actual plan without unnecessary overlap.

donts.title: Don't add mineral masses into potency
donts.detail: A combined milligram headline does not measure value, and salt weights are not elemental mineral amounts.

donts.title: Don't buy a combination by default
donts.detail: When only one nutrient needs attention, a broad formula may add unnecessary ingredients rather than practical value.

intakeGuide.summary: Use individual elemental mineral references; there is no combined ZMC requirement or exercise multiplier.

medicalGuide.summary: Condition-specific evidence, separate from sports benefits and purchase priority.

conditions.findings: Replace the deficient mineral when indicated; this does not validate every combined ZMC formula.

pathway.title: Three minerals follow separate routes
pathway.summary: Zinc, magnesium and calcium are distinct ions with their own absorption and regulation. A combination tablet does not create a shared metabolic pathway.

steps.label: Calcium is released and absorbed
steps.detail: Intestinal calcium absorption depends on the food or compound, dose and vitamin D status.

steps.label: Circulating calcium is tightly regulated
steps.detail: The body controls a small circulating calcium pool while bone holds most calcium stores.

steps.label: Calcium supports bone and signalling
steps.detail: Calcium provides bone structure and participates in muscle, nerve and other cellular signals.

steps.label: Dissolved compounds supply magnesium ions
steps.detail: The intestine absorbs a proportion of dietary magnesium; compound and dose affect availability.

steps.label: Cells use magnesium as a cofactor
steps.detail: Magnesium supports enzyme systems involved in energy metabolism and protein synthesis.

steps.label: Enzymes and ion transport sustain function
steps.detail: Magnesium-dependent processes contribute to nerve signalling and muscle contraction.

steps.label: The intestine absorbs dietary zinc
steps.detail: The absorbed fraction varies with zinc intake and meal composition, including phytate content.

steps.label: Zinc participates in cellular metabolism
steps.detail: Zinc is required for the catalytic activity of hundreds of enzymes.

steps.label: Cellular processes use available zinc
steps.detail: Zinc contributes to protein and DNA synthesis, signalling and cell division.

pathway.caveat: Parallel mineral roles do not demonstrate a special combined benefit. Compare each elemental amount and the person's need rather than the tablet's total mass.
